quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to any traffic close enough to cause a crash.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and keep going without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to any traffic close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to create a danger.

questions.question: When exiting the interstate, when should you start slowing down?

options.text: About halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you get close to the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Stay at highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to match the exit ramp's speed limit.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, turn into:

options.text: Any lane.
The first lane.
The second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: When turning, always turn into the first available legal lane in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Give the right-of-way to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction of the arrow after you yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance behind a large vehicle to:

options.text: See around the sides of the vehicle.
Stop other drivers from trying to pass.
Avoid getting caught in the vehicle's wind.

questions.correctAnswerText: See around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles block your view of the road. Increase your distance to see around them and watch the road ahead. The truck driver also may not see you directly behind them.

questions.question: In fog or mist, do not use high beams because:

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles may not see you.
Vehicles behind you will follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beams reflect back at you and reduce your visibility. Use low beams instead.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should:

options.text: Stop, listen, and go slowly.
Look both left and right to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that appear to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look both left and right to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At any place where people may cross or traffic lines meet, look to your left and right to make sure nothing is coming.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road work ahead.
Traffic light ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign means:

options.text: Yield.
Stop.
Warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: Diamond signs warn you of special conditions or hazards ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check if other drivers are moving into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Always check your blind spot over your shoulder and watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slower and less reliable.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane and speed up to match traffic flow.
Use the shoulder of the main road to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up and enter the interstate only after you find a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up and enter the interstate only after you find a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, speed up only after you see a gap in traffic. You should stay stopped while waiting for a gap to appear.

questions.question: Having a driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is both illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should return to your original lane when:

options.text: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.
You are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, move back into your original lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. This gives you enough room to safely pull back in front.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are:

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what traffic laws they must follow. They may cover direction, lane use, turning, speed, parking, or special situations. These signs are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

questions.question: Drivers must use their parking brake:

options.text: Only when parked on an incline.
Only when parked in a parking lot.
Every time they park.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time they park.
questions.explanation: Always set your parking brake when you park. Also leave the vehicle in gear for manual transmissions or in Park for automatic transmissions.

questions.question: To turn quickly, your hands should be:

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and allows you to turn safely, especially on high-speed roads.

questions.question: You should always travel:

options.text: At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.
At the speed limit.
At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should match road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never drive above the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: While driving on a roadway with a single broken white centerline:

options.text: You must stay within your lane.
You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
You may change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines between lanes mean lanes are going in the same direction. A broken white line means it is legal to pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If your vehicle is about to be hit from behind, you should NOT:

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: When hit from behind, your body moves backward. Press your head against the head restraint and brace yourself against your seat to prevent whiplash. Keep both hands on the steering wheel and be ready to brake.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can cross the center line to pass other vehicles when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Getting ____ points on your license within 24 months will result in a license suspension.

options.text: 15 points
22 points
30 points

questions.correctAnswerText: 22 points
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, driving violations add points to your license. If you get 22 points or more within 24 months, your license will be suspended. The length of suspension depends on how many violations you have had.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns drivers that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines are used to:

options.text: Mark no passing zones.
Separate lanes moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken yellow lines mean passing is allowed when it is safe.
